Reflection: I called Microtubule stabilizers (p=0.55) vs true BBBC021 Kinase inhibitors for bryostatin.

Why I was wrong: high doses showed extreme act_glcm_contrast z~29/19, tub_glcm_contrast z~10/8, stellate discohesive cells that rose monotonically rho=1.0, and the single best match was a reference of the stabilizer class sim 0.54. I over-weighted that striking cytoskeletal signal and the k-neighbour count.

What I missed: overall similarities were low 0.29-0.54 = weak evidence, and per-well NSC votes disagreed 1x stabilizer / 2x DNA damage / 1x Cholesterol-lowering. Per protocol I should have stayed with the split prior, not moved on one stain. The Microscopist favouring Actin disruptors with tubulin co-change was a clue to an upstream regulator rather than direct tubulin binder.

Biology: bryostatin is a protein kinase C activator/modulator with downstream cytoskeletal remodelling, so actin/tubulin texture mimics stabilizers. Literature: PMID 7575530 reports bryostatin-1 as protein kinase C activator; PMID 36902029 discusses PKC-delta-C1b membrane interactions.

Lesson: strong actin/tubulin z occurs in many classes; with low sims and split votes, favour upstream Kinase inhibitor and propose phospho-PKC / PKC translocation assay as follow-up.

What was right was recognizing a real dose-dependent remodeling phenotype and not following the weak 2/4 NSC majority for DNA damage, since those votes came from low-similarity wells at 0.3 and 1 uM. What was wrong was interpreting actin/tubulin texture and solidity loss as direct microtubule engagement and overweighting the single strongest NSC match of 0.537 for stabilizers at 10 uM and the stabilizer-enriched neighbour list, when downstream kinase signaling can remodel cytoskeleton secondarily.

# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_14844eef0c

Run `run_0185caa14b15` · blinded · 2026-11-01 08:37 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5-open, reference_library leave-one-MoA-out

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e2 | 10 | 1 | 249 | act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0; act_std z=+16.3; tub_glcm_contrast z=+10.6 |

## Hypothesis history

- after step 12: Microtubule stabilizers 0.50, DNA damage 0.20, Actin disruptors 0.15, Microtubule destabilizers 0.10, Cholesterol-lowering 0.05

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.55); key evidence e2, e6, e8, e9, e4.

Why: NSC split but high-dose similarity and neighbours favour stabilizers over weak DNA-damage votes; dose-monotonic cytoskeletal remodelling overrides prior.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution anti-acetylated-tubulin vs total tubulin staining plus DNA content flow cytometry for G2/M arrest to test for stabilized microtubule bundles versus actin-primary effect.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top MoA is favoured over the runner-ups: tub_mean rises dose-dependently (+2.0 at 1 µM, +5.8 at 3 µM, +6.8 at 10 µM) together with tub texture, actin texture and large-nucleus fraction. That direction fits stabilisation rather than destabilisation, and adds tubulin/nuclear effects beyond a primary actin phenotype. DNA damage is weaker than its 2/4 NSC vote suggests: those votes come from low-similarity wells (0.196 at 0.3 µM and 0.379 at 1 µM), whereas the strongest single match (0.537 at 10 µM) is stabiliser. The microscopist actin call and huge act_glcm_contrast support Actin disruptors, but no actin class appears in the neighbour lists, and actin change accompanies the marked shape/tubulin change. Acquisitions were discriminating: four doses (0.3, 1, 3, 10 µM) give monotonic actin/cell-count responses and consistent large effects at 3–10 µM, so the call is not driven by one weak well; replicate 2 at one dose would not separate stabiliser from actin better. 0.55 is suitably modest given the split atlas and dissenting phenotype read.

## Unblinding

Compound: **bryostatin** (PubChem CID [6435419](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6435419))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The call of Microtubule stabilizers was driven by the extreme high-dose cytoskeletal signal: act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 and act_std z=+16.3 at 10 uM with tub_glcm_contrast z=+10.6, persisting at 3 uM, plus monotonic dose responses for actin texture and cell loss. Unblinding revealed bryostatin, annotated here as Kinase inhibitors and known as a protein kinase C activator (PMID 7575530).

What was right was recognizing a real dose-dependent remodeling phenotype and not following the weak 2/4 NSC majority for DNA damage, since those votes came from low-similarity wells at 0.3 and 1 uM. What was wrong was interpreting actin/tubulin texture and solidity loss as direct microtubule engagement and overweighting the single strongest NSC match of 0.537 for stabilizers at 10 uM and the stabilizer-enriched neighbour list, when downstream kinase signaling can remodel cytoskeleton secondarily.

The acquisition strategy anchored on 10 uM first and sampled only 0.3-10 uM with no kinase-activity readout, so there was no test of causality. PKC-membrane interactions that can affect morphology are documented (PMID 36902029), and without a PKC-dependence or tubulin-polymer counter-assay the atlas similarity to cytoskeletal classes was misleading.

What was right:
- Detected strong dose-monotonic cytoskeletal remodeling with act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 up to z=+29.0 and dose-dependent cell loss rho=-1.00, not single-well noise
- Correctly downweighted the 2/4 NSC DNA-damage majority because similarities were weak at 0.3 uM (0.196) and 1 uM (0.379) versus 0.537 at 10 uM
- Kept actin-disruptor versus microtubule-stabilizer ambiguity on the board reflecting the microscopist actin call and mixed neighbour lists

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread massive actin texture and tub_glcm_contrast z=+10.6 plus cell_solidity z=-15.9 as direct microtubule stabilization rather than downstream PKC-driven cytoskeletal remodeling
- Overweighted the high-dose NSC match to Microtubule stabilizers and k-neighbour enrichment for stabilizers/destabilizers from compare_to_reference_atlas
- Acquired only 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with no lower-dose onset, no replicate, and no kinase-activity or tubulin-polymer assay to separate upstream kinase effect from direct cytoskeletal binding

Proposed next experiment: Treat cells with bryostatin with and without acute PKC inhibition and compare phospho-PKC substrate staining and PKC membrane translocation against direct microtubule readouts (in vitro tubulin polymerization plus acetylated versus total tubulin and phospho-histone H3 cell-cycle profile); rescue of actin texture and cell loss by PKC inhibition without direct tubulin stabilization would support upstream kinase-mediated cytoskeletal remodeling.

## Citations

Citations verified: 2/2

- PMID [7575530](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7575530/): The protein kinase C activator Bryostatin-1 induces the rapid release of TNF alpha from MONO-MAC-6 cells. *Biochem Biophys Res Commun* (1995) — Bryostatin-1 is described as a protein kinase C activator.
- PMID [36902029](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36902029/): Insertion Depth Modulates Protein Kinase C-δ-C1b Domain Interactions with Membrane Cholesterol as Revealed by MD Simulations. *Int J Mol Sci* (2023) — The PKC-delta C1b domain interacts with membrane cholesterol, linking PKC signaling to membrane organization.
